DEVANAHALLI TALUK BENGALURU RURAL DISTRICT AS PER ANNEXURE-A, DIRECT THE R2 AND 3 TO CONSIDER THE CASE OF PETITIONER AS PER SECTION 29(2) OF THE KIAD ACT, 1966 FOR DETERMINATION F COMPENSATION BY WAY OF AN AGREEMENT &
ETC.,
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER This writ petition is filed for following reliefs:
a) Issue a Writ of Certiorari to quash the General Award passed by Respondent No.3 dated 30.06.2023 bearing No.KIADB/ LAQ/2023-24 in respect of land bearing Survey no.69/2A measuring 1 acre 21 guntas situated at Byradenahalli village,
Kundana Hobli, Devenahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, , as per Annexure-A;
b) Issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the Respondents to consider the case of Petitioners as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act,, 1966 for determination of compensation by way of an agreement, etc.

2. Sri Varun R.R. learned counsel for petitioner submitted that land bearing Sy.no.69/2A,
measuring 01 acre 21 guntas situated at Byradenahalli village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk,
Bengaluru Rural District, originally belonged to petitioner's father one Sri. Doddaanjinappa @
Anjinappa @ Anjini and revenue records were standing in his name.

It was NC: 2023:KHC:40680 submitted that respondents - authority had initiated acquisition of aforesaid land for purpose of ITIR project and issued Final Notification dated 25.05.2022 and petitioner submitted representation for disbursement of compensation.
It was submitted that though petitioner was entitled to higher compensation under consent award, General Award was passed by respondent no.3, which was under challenge.
It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court allowed several writ petitions, including W.P.No.6198/2015 disposed of on 25.08.2015.

Relying Sri Appajigowda vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58902433/
2 upon same, sought for granting similar relief.

sentences.text:
3. On other hand, Sri Manjunath V Rayappa, learned AGA for respondent no.1 and Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that in view of earlier decision, respondent no.3 would consider representation, in accordance with law and sought for disposal of writ petition.
4.
Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.

5. From above, it is seen that in W.P.No.6198/2015 contention of petitioner therein about failure to provide NC: 2023:KHC:40680 opportunity to accept compensation under consent award which was higher than under General award was upheld and this Court set aside General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's representation for passing consent award.
Said decision would squarely apply in this case.

6. Accordingly, Writ petition is disposed of, impugned General Award bearing No.KIADB/LAQ/2023-24 dated 30.06.2023 at Annexure-A passed by respondent no.3 in respect of land bearing Survey no.69/2A, measuring 01 acre 21 guntas situated at Byradenahalli village,
Kundana Hobli, Devenahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, is hereby set aside.
Respondent no.3 shall consider petitioner's representation and pass appropriate orders thereon within a period of eight weeks.

Needless to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as a positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as a direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law.
Sd/-
